title: Brr Brr Patapim
blurb: Brr Brr Patapim — the tree-legged forest creature with a bafflingly detailed Italian backstory, and one of the most beloved characters in the Italian brainrot universe. The rhythm of the name alone is why it spread: it's fun to say, impossible to forget, and means absolutely nothing. Play it to summon anyone under fifteen instantly.
origin: An Italian brainrot AI character in the Tralalero Tralala universe.

title: Bombardiro Crocodilo
blurb: Bombardiro Crocodilo — a crocodile fused with a bomber plane, delivered in that unmistakable Italian brainrot narration. It is one of the genre's most recognisable characters and a perfect illustration of the whole movement: nobody asked for a flying crocodile, nobody can explain it, and yet here we all are, several billion views later.
origin: One of the flagship Italian brainrot AI characters.

title: Trippi Troppi
blurb: Trippi Troppi — another entry in the Italian brainrot bestiary, with the genre's signature blend of nonsense naming and confident narration. The formula is simple and unstoppable: give an AI-generated creature a rhyming Italian-adjacent name, narrate its lore with total sincerity, and let the internet do the rest.
origin: An Italian brainrot AI character.

title: Udin Din Din Dun
blurb: Udin Din Din Dun — pure rhythmic nonsense from the brainrot canon, built entirely out of repeated syllables and confidence. It works the way a nursery rhyme works: the meaning is irrelevant, the cadence does everything. Play it once and it will loop in your head for the rest of the afternoon. Sorry in advance.
origin: A rhythmic Italian brainrot chant.

title: Ballerina Cappuccina
blurb: Ballerina Cappuccina — a ballerina with a cappuccino cup for a head, because the Italian brainrot universe follows dream logic exclusively. She's one of the genre's most-shared characters, and the sing-song delivery of her name is a large part of why. Coffee, dance, and absolute nonsense, in perfect harmony.
origin: An Italian brainrot AI character — the coffee-cup ballerina.

title: Cappuccino Assassino
blurb: Cappuccino Assassino — the killer coffee, and companion character to Ballerina Cappuccina in the brainrot extended universe. The genre has produced an entire coffee-based faction, which is either a commentary on Italian culture or simply what happens when an AI is asked to invent characters at 3am. Both readings are correct.
origin: An Italian brainrot AI character — the assassin cappuccino.

title: Chicken Jockey
blurb: CHICKEN JOCKEY! — the two words that turned cinema screenings into riots. When A Minecraft Movie hit theatres, this line triggered synchronised chaos worldwide: popcorn airborne, kids standing on seats, staff considering new careers. It became the defining cinema-behaviour meme of the year. Play it responsibly, ideally not in a cinema.
origin: From A Minecraft Movie (2025) — the line that caused worldwide cinema chaos.

title: Low Taper Fade
blurb: 'The low taper fade meme is still massive' — the line that outlived its own moment by a spectacular margin. What began as a joke about Ninja's haircut became a self-referential monument: a meme about how big the meme still is. It is peak internet recursion, and it refuses to die. Still massive, apparently.
origin: From the Ninja low taper fade meme — the joke that became about its own longevity.

title: FEIN FEIN FEIN
blurb: FEIN FEIN FEIN — the chant from Travis Scott's track that mutated into one of the internet's most aggressive hype sounds. It's rave energy compressed into a single repeated syllable, deployed in edits whenever intensity needs to peak. Genuinely useful for gym content, and genuinely unbearable at close range. Both by design.
origin: From Travis Scott's 'FE!N', adopted as an all-purpose hype chant.

title: Chill Guy
blurb: The Chill Guy theme — soundtrack to the unbothered dog in a grey sweater who became the internet's mascot for radical acceptance. My new character is a chill guy: he has problems, he simply does not engage with them. Play it when you decide, correctly, that something is not worth your energy.
origin: From the viral 'Chill Guy' character meme.

title: SYBAU
blurb: SYBAU — the acronym that took over comment sections, standing for something considerably less polite than 'please stop talking'. It's the brainrot era's favourite conversation ender: fast to type, faster to say, and universally understood by anyone under twenty. Deploy when a discussion has clearly run its course.
origin: A viral Gen Alpha acronym used to shut down conversations.

title: SHEESH
blurb: SHEEEESH — the drawn-out exclamation of being genuinely impressed, and one of the defining slang sounds of the decade. Length equals sincerity: a short sheesh is polite acknowledgement, a five-second sheesh means someone has done something legitimately remarkable. Play it for flexes, feats, and outfits that go unreasonably hard.
origin: The viral 'sheesh' exclamation of admiration.

title: Maxwell the Cat Theme
blurb: The Maxwell the Cat theme — the frantic fiddle tune attached to a 3D cat spinning eternally. Maxwell has been placed into every video game, every music video, and every corner of the internet, always spinning, always accompanied by this song. It's the purest form of meme: no joke, no context, just a cat and a fiddle.
origin: The theme attached to the viral spinning Maxwell the Cat 3D model.

title: Bazinga
blurb: BAZINGA — Sheldon Cooper's catchphrase, adopted by the internet with maximum irony. It's now used exclusively to mock the concept of a catchphrase: play it after the worst possible joke, ideally one that nobody laughed at. The word has completed a full journey from sincere sitcom punchline to universal cringe artefact.
origin: Sheldon Cooper's catchphrase from The Big Bang Theory, adopted ironically.

title: Bonk
blurb: BONK — the sharp cartoon thwack of immediate correction, most famously wielded by a bat-carrying Cheems. It's the internet's disciplinary tool for cursed thoughts and questionable posts. One bonk, no discussion, straight to horny jail. The sound is the entire justice system.
origin: The corrective cartoon bonk of the Cheems bat meme.

title: Side Eye
blurb: The side-eye sound — a sting of pure silent judgement. Where our bombastic side eye is theatrical, this one is subtle: the glance you give across a room when someone says something questionable and you're saving the comment for later. Play it whenever a look would say more than words.
origin: The audio sting of a judgmental sideways glance.

title: Somebody Toucha My Spaghet
blurb: 'Somebody toucha my spaghet!' — the outraged cry of a man whose pasta has been violated. It's a foundational text of absurdist meme culture from the golden age of YouTube Poop, and it remains funny for reasons nobody has ever satisfactorily explained. Play it when anyone touches anything of yours.
origin: From the classic 'somebody toucha my spaghet' meme.

title: Nice
blurb: 'Nice.' — deadpan approval, the internet's favourite one-word review. It's the correct response to anything mildly satisfying, any number ending in 69, and any achievement that doesn't warrant real enthusiasm. Understated by design: the flatness is what makes it funny. Nice.
origin: The deadpan 'nice' approval clip.

title: Wow (Owen Wilson)
blurb: 'Wow.' — Owen Wilson's signature exclamation, extracted from decades of film and compiled by the internet into its own genre. It's the most laid-back expression of astonishment ever recorded: mild, sincere, and applicable to literally anything. There are supercuts of this containing hundreds of instances. Wow.
origin: Owen Wilson's signature 'wow', an internet institution.

title: Triggered
blurb: The TRIGGERED sound — the distorted alarm that accompanied a thousand shaking-red-filter reaction images. It defined an entire era of meme aesthetics, when overreaction was the joke and every minor annoyance became a full meltdown. Play it when someone's composure visibly departs. Vintage internet, still effective.
origin: The sting from the classic 'triggered' reaction meme format.

title: RUN
blurb: RUN. — one syllable, total urgency, no further information provided. It's the internet's evacuation order, and its power comes from the ambiguity: you don't know what's coming, only that leaving is now the priority. Play it over anything approaching, escalating, or generally going wrong at speed.
origin: The viral one-word evacuation clip.

title: Leeroy Jenkins
blurb: LEEEEROY JENKINSSS — the battle cry that ruined a meticulously-planned World of Warcraft raid in 2005 and became one of the internet's founding legends. It's the sound of abandoning strategy entirely in favour of enthusiasm. Play it before any reckless charge into a situation nobody prepared for. At least he has chicken.
origin: From the legendary 2005 World of Warcraft raid video.

title: This Is Sparta
blurb: THIS IS SPARTA! — Gerard Butler's roar from 300, followed in the film by a kick down a very deep hole. The internet adopted it as the ultimate declaration of territory and the standard soundtrack for pushing someone (metaphorically) into a pit. Remains one of the most-quoted movie lines of the internet era.
origin: King Leonidas's line from 300 (2006).

title: WOMBO COMBO
blurb: 'OH! WOMBO COMBO!' — the ecstatic commentary from a legendary Super Smash Bros. tournament clip that became gaming's original hype meme. The pure, cracking-voiced joy of it is timeless. Play it when anything chains together perfectly: combos, plans, or a sequence of events that shouldn't have worked but did.
origin: From the legendary Super Smash Bros. Melee 'Wombo Combo' clip.

title: Bird Is the Word
blurb: 'Have you heard? The bird is the word.' — Peter Griffin's obsession with Surfin' Bird became one of Family Guy's most enduring meme exports. The repetition is the point: it's designed to be maddening, and it succeeds completely. Play it until everyone in the room has heard about the bird.
origin: From Family Guy's Surfin' Bird episode.

title: Burger King Foot Lettuce
blurb: 'The Burger King foot lettuce. The last thing you'd want in your Burger King burger is someone's foot fungus.' — the robotic text-to-speech reading of a Top 15 list that became one of the internet's most quoted passages. An entire generation can recite this from memory. Nobody knows why. Everybody can.
origin: From the viral TTS 'Top 15 Rage Comics' video.

title: It's Over 9000
blurb: 'IT'S OVER NINE THOUSAAAAND!' — Vegeta's scouter-shattering announcement, and one of the oldest memes still in active circulation. It's the universal way to say a number is absurdly high, whether you're describing power levels, temperatures, or how many times you've rewatched something. A genuine internet fossil, still fully operational.
origin: Vegeta's iconic power-level line from Dragon Ball Z.

title: My Name Is Jeff
blurb: 'My name is Jeff.' — delivered with the confidence of a man who has never once introduced himself successfully. From 22 Jump Street, it became the internet's favourite way to introduce anyone, especially when the name is obviously wrong. Play it during introductions to derail them permanently.
origin: Channing Tatum's line from 22 Jump Street (2014).

title: Kool-Aid Man OH YEAH
blurb: OH YEAAAAH! — the Kool-Aid Man, arriving through a load-bearing wall as always. He has never once used a door and shows no interest in learning. Play it for unexpected entrances, uninvited opinions, and anyone who joins a conversation with maximum property damage. Structurally irresponsible, spiritually correct.
origin: The Kool-Aid Man's iconic wall-smashing catchphrase.

title: Directed by Michael Bay
blurb: 'Directed by Michael Bay' — the credit sting that turns any chaotic moment into a blockbuster. The joke writes itself: something explodes, something flips, someone walks away without looking back, and this plays. It's the internet's way of awarding an ordinary disaster a two-hundred-million-dollar budget.
origin: The meme credit sting applied to explosive real-life moments.

title: Bing Chilling
blurb: '冰淇淋' — John Cena's Mandarin ice cream monologue, delivered with such committed enthusiasm that it became one of the internet's most quoted clips. Very good, very nice. The genuine joy in his delivery is what elevated it from a promotional video to a permanent cultural artefact. Bing chilling.
origin: John Cena's viral Mandarin ice cream video.

title: Sonic Ring
blurb: The Sonic ring collect — a bright metallic chime that thirty years of players associate with not dying. Every ring is one more chance, and this sound is the sound of buying it. Play it for small saves, near-misses, and any moment where you technically got away with something.
origin: The ring collection sound from Sonic the Hedgehog (Sega).

title: Minecraft TNT
blurb: The Minecraft TNT hiss and blast — the sound of a decision that cannot be undone. Whether you're mining efficiently or griefing a friend's build, the fuse gives you exactly enough time to regret it. Play it when something is about to go irreversibly wrong, which in Minecraft is most of the time.
origin: The TNT fuse and explosion from Minecraft (Mojang).

title: Minecraft Creeper
blurb: The creeper hiss — gaming's most feared warning sound. That soft ssssss means you have roughly one second to react and your build has roughly zero. It's the single most effective jump-scare Mojang ever created, and it still works on veterans two decades later. Aww man.
origin: The creeper hiss and explosion from Minecraft (Mojang).

title: Minecraft Level Up
blurb: The Minecraft level-up chime — that bright, ascending sparkle that means you can finally enchant something. It's one of gaming's most satisfying progression sounds, engineered to make grinding feel worthwhile. Play it whenever you achieve anything, from a promotion to successfully getting out of bed.
origin: The level-up sound from Minecraft (Mojang).

title: Minecraft Enderman
blurb: The Enderman vwoop — the reversed, unsettling noise of a tall creature deciding you looked at it wrong. Minecraft's sound design turns simple audio into genuine dread, and this is the best example: harmless until you make eye contact, then absolutely not harmless. Don't look up.
origin: The Enderman ambient and teleport sound from Minecraft.

title: Minecraft Ghast
blurb: The Ghast cry — a sound Mojang famously created from a sleeping cat, and which somehow became one of the most haunting noises in gaming. Echoing across the Nether, it means fireballs are inbound from something enormous and floating. Cute origin story, genuinely terrifying result.
origin: The Ghast cry from Minecraft's Nether — originally recorded from a cat.

title: Valorant Ace
blurb: The Valorant ace sting — the announcement that one player eliminated the entire enemy team. It's the highest individual honour the game hands out, and the sound is appropriately triumphant. Play it after any solo achievement, particularly one that should have required help.
origin: The ace announcement from Valorant (Riot Games).

title: Emergency Meeting
blurb: EMERGENCY MEETING — the alarm that stops everything and forces everyone to explain themselves. Among Us made this the universal sound for 'we need to talk right now', and it works perfectly in real life: play it when the group chat needs urgent moderation or someone has to answer for something.
origin: The emergency meeting alarm from Among Us (InnerSloth).

title: Geometry Dash Death
blurb: The Geometry Dash death sound — heard, on average, several hundred times per level. It's the audio signature of rage-inducing precision platforming: brief, blunt, and immediately followed by another attempt. Play it for repeated failures, especially ones you're about to repeat again.
origin: The death sound from Geometry Dash.

title: Pac-Man Death
blurb: The Pac-Man death sound — that descending warble of a yellow circle meeting a ghost. It's been signalling failure since 1980, making it one of the oldest fail sounds in gaming. Play it for defeats that feel retro, inevitable, and slightly your own fault for going down that corridor.
origin: The death sound from Pac-Man (Namco, 1980).

title: Mario Pipe
blurb: The Mario pipe warp — the descending bloop of disappearing into plumbing. It's the sound of a quick exit to somewhere else entirely, which makes it perfect for leaving conversations, ducking out of plans, and any escape that should look effortless. Down the pipe, problem solved.
origin: The pipe warp sound from Super Mario Bros. (Nintendo).

title: Duolingo Correct
blurb: The Duolingo correct chime — the bright little reward that keeps five hundred million people doing language exercises. It's one of the most effective dopamine loops ever shipped in an app. Play it whenever you get anything right, and feel your streak spiritually extend by one day.
origin: Duolingo's correct-answer chime.

title: Duolingo Wrong
blurb: The Duolingo wrong-answer buzz — a small sound carrying enormous disappointment, because you know the owl saw that. It's the counterpart to the correct chime, and the reason a green bird has become the internet's most feared authority figure. Play it when someone gets something confidently wrong.
origin: Duolingo's incorrect-answer sound.

title: FitnessGram Pacer Test
blurb: 'The FitnessGram Pacer Test is a multi-stage aerobic capacity test...' — the announcement that struck fear into every school gymnasium in America. It's a shared trauma so universal it became a meme, and an entire generation can recite the opening verbatim while feeling their lungs preemptively burn.
origin: The narration from the school FitnessGram Pacer Test.

title: Windows XP Startup
blurb: The Windows XP startup chime — four seconds of pure early-2000s optimism, composed by Bill Brown and heard by more people than most symphonies. It means the family computer is ready and the dial-up is about to be occupied. One of the most nostalgic sounds in computing history.
origin: The boot chime from Microsoft Windows XP (2001).

title: Windows 7 Startup
blurb: The Windows 7 startup sound — the sleeker, more confident successor to XP's chime, and the soundtrack to computing's most beloved operating system. Windows 7 nostalgia runs deep, and this four-note flourish is its anthem. Play it to summon anyone who still resents every version since.
origin: The boot sound from Microsoft Windows 7 (2009).

title: Xbox 360 Startup
blurb: The Xbox 360 startup — the swooshing green orb of an entire console generation. It meant Halo nights, Live parties, and a very real chance of a red ring. For millions it's the sound of adolescence, and it still triggers instant nostalgia for a time when games came on discs.
origin: The boot sound from the Xbox 360 (Microsoft, 2005).

title: PS4 Startup
blurb: The PlayStation 4 startup — a smooth, modern boot chime that says the evening's plans are now finalised. It lacks the drama of the PS1's orchestral warning but makes up for it in polish. Play it when settling in for something you have absolutely no intention of leaving early.
origin: The boot sound from the PlayStation 4 (Sony, 2013).

title: PlayStation Startup
blurb: The original PlayStation startup — that ominous, ethereal swell that told an entire generation the disc had read successfully. Gamers still recall the specific dread of hearing it stutter. It's one of the most atmospheric boot sequences ever made, for a console that mostly played football games.
origin: The boot sequence from the original PlayStation (Sony, 1994).

title: Nokia Ringtone
blurb: The Nokia tune — mathematically one of the most-heard melodies in human history, having rung from billions of indestructible handsets. It's a 19th-century guitar piece by Francisco Tárrega that accidentally became the sound of the mobile era. Play it in public and watch everyone over thirty check their pocket.
origin: Nokia's default ringtone, adapted from Tárrega's 'Gran Vals' (1902).

title: Dial-Up Modem
blurb: The dial-up handshake — thirty seconds of shrieking negotiation that stood between you and the internet, and which absolutely could not happen while anyone was on the phone. For anyone who lived through it, this sound is pure sense-memory. For everyone else, it's inexplicable machine screaming.
origin: The 56k modem connection handshake.

title: You've Got Mail (AOL)
blurb: 'You've got mail!' — three words that once genuinely made people excited to check their inbox, a feeling now entirely lost to history. AOL's greeting became so iconic it got a Tom Hanks film named after it. Play it for anyone who remembers when email was a treat rather than a burden.
origin: AOL's iconic email notification.

title: Facebook Notification
blurb: The Facebook notification pop — the sound that ran social media for a decade before the feed swallowed everything. It still triggers a small reflex in anyone who was online between 2008 and 2016. Play it as a nostalgia hit, or to convince someone their aunt has commented on a photo.
origin: Facebook's notification sound.

title: Messenger Notification
blurb: The Messenger notification — the distinctive pop that means a conversation has started whether you wanted one or not. It sits alongside WhatsApp and iMessage in the tiny group of sounds recognised by billions of people. Add it to the notification-prank arsenal; it never misses.
origin: Facebook Messenger's message alert.

title: TikTok Notification
blurb: The TikTok notification — the alert of the app that reorganised global attention spans. It means someone liked something, or the algorithm has decided you need to come back. Play it near anyone under thirty to trigger an immediate, involuntary phone check. Devastatingly effective.
origin: TikTok's notification alert.

title: Windows 11 Notification
blurb: The Windows 11 notification — softer and more polite than its predecessors, in keeping with an operating system that would very much like you to try Edge. It's the modern face of a sound family stretching back to the 90s. Play it for gentle interruptions and unwanted software suggestions.
origin: Microsoft Windows 11's notification sound.

title: R2-D2
blurb: R2-D2's beeps and whistles — the most expressive language ever built out of pure electronic noise. Ben Burtt created a character who communicates complex emotion without a single word, and audiences understood every line. Play it to respond to anything without committing to an actual opinion.
origin: R2-D2's vocalisations from Star Wars, designed by Ben Burtt.

title: Lightsaber Ignition
blurb: The lightsaber ignition — that snap-hiss of a plasma blade coming to life, built by Ben Burtt from a projector motor hum and a broken TV picking up interference. It's arguably the most famous sound effect ever created. Play it when drawing any weapon, including a strongly-worded reply.
origin: The lightsaber ignition from Star Wars, created by Ben Burtt.

title: Hello There
blurb: 'Hello there!' — Obi-Wan Kenobi's greeting, and the single most reliable way to identify a prequel-memes enjoyer in the wild. Say it in any room and someone will answer 'GENERAL KENOBI' without hesitation. It's a password, a greeting, and a personality test rolled into one.
origin: Obi-Wan Kenobi's greeting from Revenge of the Sith, a prequel-meme cornerstone.

title: Chewbacca Roar
blurb: The Chewbacca roar — a Wookiee's full emotional range, assembled from bears, walruses, and badgers by Ben Burtt. It expresses frustration, affection, and mild disagreement using the same sound, which is honestly relatable. Play it when words fail and only a roar will do.
origin: Chewbacca's vocalisations from Star Wars, built from real animal recordings.

title: Noot Noot (Pingu)
blurb: NOOT NOOT — Pingu's declaration, and a foundational sound of absurdist internet humour. The claymation penguin's honking became a whole language: greeting, protest, and punchline all at once. It has survived every meme cycle since 2012 by virtue of being genuinely funny. Noot noot.
origin: Pingu's iconic 'noot noot' from the claymation series.

title: Squid Game Doll
blurb: The Squid Game doll's song — 'mugunghwa kkoci pieotseumnida' — sung sweetly before the shooting starts. It's the most unsettling nursery rhyme on television, and it triggered a global wave of playground Red Light Green Light. Play it and watch everyone in the room freeze instinctively.
origin: The doll's Red Light, Green Light song from Squid Game.

title: Squid Game Green Light
blurb: The Squid Game green-light cue — the signal to move, and the brief window before everything goes wrong again. Netflix's biggest show ever turned a schoolyard game into global shorthand for high-stakes pressure. Use it to start a race, a task, or any activity where hesitation is fatal.
origin: The Red Light, Green Light game cue from Squid Game.

title: Crab Rave
blurb: Crab Rave — the tropical house drop that became the internet's official celebration of things ending. Something bad got cancelled? Crab rave. Someone's downfall arrived? Crab rave. Noisestorm's track plus dancing crustaceans created the most joyful schadenfreude anthem ever produced.
origin: Noisestorm's 'Crab Rave' (Monstercat), the internet's celebration anthem.
